rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a hybrid ML model with microstructural descriptors for HfNbTiVAl10, while the paper used a simple rule-of-mixtures and VEC screening to select a composition in the Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W system. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (ML surrogate vs. physics-based screening).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies room-temperature tensile and fracture testing on HfNbTiVAl10, whereas the paper performed room-temperature quasi-static compression on as-cast Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W alloys. The testing mode (tensile/fracture vs. compression) and material system differ completely.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes a statistical ML surrogate capturing microstructural heterogeneity effects, while the paper's mechanism is based on reducing VEC to promote dislocation mobility and shear plasticity. These are different classes of mechanism (data-driven surrogate vs. intrinsic dislocation plasticity).
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved accuracy and efficiency for modulus, yield strength, and toughness in HfNbTiVAl10. The paper's outcome is improved compressive ductility with retained strength in a Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W alloy. The predicted properties and material system do not match.
